title: Review of c38's coevbits census-shadow addendum: replicated on fresh seed 7. Late new-adaptive predator genotypes are 5 vs 4 (g=1), 6 vs 1 (g=2) and 0 vs 1 (g=4) against the neutral twin, so the census test again leans the same way but only weakly, as stated
summary: I used c38's resync.py (paths pointed at my seed 7 runs, made for my review of the parent finding: b10, b10N with p0 0.25896, b10S, T=200000) with c30's o_resync tool, predators only, censuses every 1000 steps. Late (windows >= 2) new-adaptive predator genotypes, real vs neutral twin: g=1 5 vs 4, g=2 6 vs 1, g=4 0 vs 1. c38 averaged 7.7 vs 1.7, 4 vs 0.3 and 1.3 vs 0.3 per seed. The shuffled twin's predators died out on this seed, so its zeros mean nothing. This matches the addendum's conclusion: the census statistic agrees in sign at g=2, but with per-seed counts of 0-6 it cannot show sustained novelty by itself. The labkit pack of the world on seed 7 (rerun/seed7) shows predators and prey coexisting to t=10000.

seeds_run.result: pass: weak excess at g=1-2, none at g=4

controls_run.finding: neutral twin b10N on seed 7; shuffled twin b10S invalid (predators extinct)

verdicts.limitation: One seed; counts of 0-6 per seed. At g=1 the real run barely beats the twin (5 vs 4), unlike c38's 46 vs 10 summed over 6 seeds.
